publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: End to End Learning for Self-Driving Cars

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: We trained a convolutional neural network (CNN) to map raw pixels from a single front-facing camera directly to steering commands.

span.label: end-to-end learning of lane and road following
span.quote: We have empirically demonstrated that CNNs are able to learn the entire task of lane and road following without manual decomposition into road or lane marking detection, semantic abstraction, path planning, and control.

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: Evaluating our networks is done in two steps, first in simulation, and then in on-road tests.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the steering command is stored as 1/r rather than r, which removes the singularity at straight-ahead and makes the label continuous through zero across left and right turns
span.quote: In order to make our system independent of the car geometry, we represent the steering command as 1/r where r is the turning radius in meters. We use 1/r instead of r to prevent a singularity when driving straight (the turning radius for driving straight is infinity). 1/r smoothly transitions through zero from left turns (negative values) to right turns (positive values).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: recovery is taught rather than encountered: the training set is augmented with images of the car already displaced from the lane centre, because human driving alone never shows the network a mistake
span.quote: Training with data from only the human driver is not sufficient. The network must learn how to recover from mistakes. Otherwise the car will slowly drift off the road. The training data is therefore augmented with additional images that show the car in different shifts from the center of the lane and rotations from the direction of the road.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: off-centre viewpoints are synthesised under an approximation the paper states it knows to be wrong - everything below the horizon treated as flat ground, everything above it as infinitely far - accepted because the resulting distortions do not hurt training
span.quote: Precise viewpoint transformation requires 3D scene knowledge which we don’t have. We therefore approximate the transformation by assuming all points below the horizon are on flat ground and all points above the horizon are infinitely far away. This works fine for flat terrain but it introduces distortions for objects that stick above the ground, such as cars, poles, trees, and buildings. Fortunately these distortions don’t pose a big problem for network training.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the label for a synthesised viewpoint is not the driver's command but the command that would return the car to the correct place within a fixed two-second horizon
span.quote: The steering label for transformed images is adjusted to one that would steer the vehicle back to the desired location and orientation in two seconds.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the training frames are filtered by the driver's activity label and then downsampled, because consecutive frames at full rate are near-duplicates
span.quote: To train a CNN to do lane following we only select data where the driver was staying in a lane and discard the rest. We then sample that video at 10 FPS. A higher sampling rate would result in including images that are highly similar and thus not provide much useful information.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the perturbations are drawn from a normal distribution deliberately twice as wide as the variation measured in human drivers
span.quote: The magnitude of these perturbations is chosen randomly from a normal distribution. The distribution has zero mean, and the standard deviation is twice the standard deviation that we measured with human drivers.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: autonomy is computed from a COUNTED event and an ASSUMED constant: each simulated intervention is charged a fixed six seconds of human takeover time
span.quote: We assume that in real life an actual intervention would require a total of six seconds: this is the time required for a human to retake control of the vehicle, re-center it, and then restart the self-steering mode.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the normalisation layer is inside the network but hard-coded, so it is not learned and can be changed with the architecture and run on the GPU
span.quote: The first layer of the network performs image normalization. The normalizer is hard-coded and is not adjusted in the learning process. Performing normalization in the network allows the normalization scheme to be altered with the network architecture and to be accelerated via GPU processing.

span.label: more work is needed to improve robustness and to verify/visualize the network's internal processing
span.quote: More work is needed to improve the robustness of the network

span.label: The viewpoint transformation used for augmentation is an approximation because the true 3D scene geometry is unknown.
span.quote: Precise viewpoint transformation requires 3D scene knowledge which we don’t have.

span.label: That approximation distorts objects standing above the ground plane.
span.quote: This works fine for flat terrain but it introduces distortions for objects that stick above the ground, such as cars, poles, trees, and buildings.

span.label: Larger augmentation magnitudes introduce undesirable artifacts into the training data.
span.quote: Artificially augmenting the data does add undesirable artifacts as the magnitude increases (see Section 2).

span.label: Robustness of the network, methods to verify it, and internal-state visualisation all remain open.
span.quote: More work is needed to improve the robustness of the network, to find methods to verify the robustness, and to improve visualization of the network-internal processing steps.

span.label: The results are explicitly preliminary.
span.quote: This paper describes preliminary results of this new effort.

span.label: The reported autonomy percentage is built on an assumed six-second cost per intervention, which the authors state as an assumption rather than measure.
span.quote: We assume that in real life an actual intervention would require a total of six seconds: this is the time required for a human to retake control of the vehicle, re-center it, and then restart the self-steering mode

span.label: An intervention is a threshold crossing in simulation, not a human decision: the car counts as having failed when it passes one metre from the centre line.
span.quote: These interventions occur when the simulated vehicle departs from the center line by more than one meter

span.label: After every simulated intervention the car is placed back on the recorded ground truth, so the measure cannot observe how a failure would have developed.
span.quote: a virtual human intervention is triggered, and the virtual vehicle position and orientation is reset to match the ground truth of the corresponding frame of the original test video

span.label: The training set is deliberately not the driving distribution: one driver activity is kept, the rest discarded, and curves are then over-represented on purpose.
span.quote: To train a CNN to do lane following we only select data where the driver was staying in a lane and discard the rest. We then sample that video at 10 FPS. A higher sampling rate would result in including images that are highly similar and thus not provide much useful information. 4 Center cameraCNNNetwork computed steering commandDrive by wire interface Figure 4: CNN architecture. The network has about 27 million connections and 250 thousand parameters. To remove a bias towards driving straight the training data includes a higher proportion of frames that represent road curves

span.label: manually calibrating the lane centre for each frame used by the simulator, rather than taking the human driver's position as the target
span.quote: Since human drivers might not be driving in the center of the lane all the time, we manually calibrate the lane center associated with each frame in the video used by the simulator.

span.label: convolutional neural network
span.quote: We trained a convolutional neural network (CNN) to map raw pixels from a single front-facing camera directly to steering commands

span.label: autonomy
span.quote: We estimate what percentage of the time the network could drive the car (autonomy). The metric is determined by counting simulated human interventions

span.label: intervention
span.quote: These interventions occur when the simulated vehicle departs from the center line by more than one meter

span.label: road features
span.quote: The system automatically learns internal representations of the necessary processing steps such as detecting useful road features

span.label: training signal
span.quote: with only the human steering angle as the training signal

span.label: autonomy - AS A STIPULATED FORMULA: one minus the intervention count times six seconds over elapsed time, as a percentage; the word names an arithmetic result, not an observed capability
span.quote: We calculate the percentage autonomy by counting the number of interventions, multiplying by 6 seconds, dividing by the elapsed time of the simulated test, and then subtracting the result from 1

span.label: a performance criterion - CHOSEN FOR LEGIBILITY, WHICH IS NOT THE SAME AS BEING RIGHT: the paper's argument for end-to-end training is that human-selected intermediate criteria are picked because a person can interpret them, and that this does not guarantee system performance
span.quote: instead of optimizing human-selected intermediate criteria, e. g., lane detection. Such criteria understandably are selected for ease of human interpretation which doesn’t automatically guarantee maximum system performance

span.label: road features - LEARNED WITHOUT EVER BEING NAMED: the network detects them from the steering angle alone, and the authors state they never trained it to detect road outlines
span.quote: The system automatically learns internal representations of the necessary processing steps such as detecting useful road features with only the human steering angle as the training signal. We never explicitly trained it to detect, for example, the outline of roads

span.label: builds-on → Pomerleau ALVINN (1989)
span.quote: In many ways, DAVE-2 was inspired by the pioneering work of Pomerleau [6] who in 1989 built the Autonomous Land Vehicle in a Neural Network (ALVINN) system.

span.label: builds-on → DARPA Autonomous Vehicle (DAVE) [5]
span.quote: The groundwork for this project was done over 10 years ago in a Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) seedling project known as DARPA Autonomous Vehicle (DAVE) [5] in which a sub-scale radio control (RC) car drove through a junk-filled alley way.

span.label: builds-on → Pomerleau [6], the ALVINN system
span.quote: In many ways, DAVE-2 was inspired by the pioneering work of Pomerleau [6] who in 1989 built the Autonomous Land Vehicle in a Neural Network (ALVINN) system.

span.label: extends → Pomerleau [6], the ALVINN system
span.quote: Our work differs in that 25 years of advances let us apply far more data and computational power to the task.

span.label: autonomy —operationalised-as→ intervention
span.quote: We estimate what percentage of the time the network could drive the car (autonomy). The metric is determined by counting simulated human interventions

span.label: training signal —causes→ road features
span.quote: The system automatically learns internal representations of the necessary processing steps such as detecting useful road features with only the human steering angle as the training signal

span.label: 98% — fraction of time the network drove autonomously (Holmdel to Atlantic Highlands)
span.quote: we are autonomous approximately 98% of the time

span.label: 30 — system operating frame rate
span.quote: The system operates at 30 frames per second (FPS).

span.label: 9 — network depth: 1 normalization + 5 convolutional + 3 fully connected
span.quote: The network consists of 9 layers, including a normalization layer, 5 convolutional layers and 3 fully connected layers.

span.label: 10 — distance driven on the Garden State Parkway with zero interventions
span.quote: We also drove 10 miles on the Garden State Parkway (a multi-lane divided highway with on and off ramps) with zero intercepts.

span.label: An end-to-end CNN mapping raw front-camera pixels directly to steering commands learned to drive on local roads and highways with ~98% autonomy, without hand-coded lane detection or path planning.
span.quote: We trained a convolutional neural network (CNN) to map raw pixels from a single front-facing camera directly to steering commands. This end-to-end approach proved surprisingly powerful.

span.label: The network learned useful road features using only the human steering angle as the training signal, never explicitly supervised to detect them.
span.quote: detecting useful road features with only the human steering angle as the training signal. We never explicitly trained it to detect, for example, the outline of roads.

span.label: raw camera pixels
span.quote: map raw pixels from a single front-facing camera directly to steering commands

span.label: steering angle
span.quote: only the human steering angle as the training signal

span.label: autonomy
span.quote: estimate what percentage of the time the network could drive the car (autonomy)

span.label: autonomy (metric)
span.quote: estimate what percentage of the time the network could drive the car (autonomy). The metric is determined by counting simulated human interventions

span.label: end-to-end learning
span.quote: our end-to-end system optimizes all processing steps simultaneously

span.label: standard-deviation
span.quote: The distribution has zero mean, and the standard deviation is twice the standard deviation that we measured with human drivers.
